card_title: Independent verification that the T1-1 / T1-2 rulings are landed
nature: RULING-LANDING VERIFICATION. Not an implementation. Not a promotion. Not a countersignature.
status_note: This card does NOT change any product-card status. I-06-A remains blocked; the rev2 candidate remains UNRATIFIED.

what_the_rulings_say.T1-1: D-W06 OPEN-2 option A -- the idempotency key MUST include the request identity (source_sha256 + review_policy + role_set + request identity, where request identity covers as_of_date / target / payload digest). Option B (keep the key, fail-closed on same-key-different-payload) is REJECTED.
what_the_rulings_say.T1-2: D-W06 OPEN-1 option A -- single persistent owner is the CW store (src/company_wiki/source_catalog/store.py, catalog.sqlite3, additive tables via the existing _apply_additive_migrations). The attempt's option-B shape (separate internal SQLite file) is NOT adopted. OPEN-3 -- claim(owner, lease_seconds) stays an explicit single-shot authorisation; workers are not auto-resumed.
what_the_rulings_say.still_other_parties: OPEN-4 (review method / reviewer binding / receipt invalidation) -- wiki source-review owner + security reviewer. OPEN-5 (consumer & recovery interface) -- RF consumer owner. OPEN-6 (not_detected vs detected_and_ignored ownership) -- security reviewer. These are NOT decided by this card and NOT decided by T1-1/T1-2.

finding: The rulings were ALREADY LANDED at round 41, inside I-06-A/a20260919-01. No T1-1/T1-2 card directory existed, but the revised candidate, a pre-frozen oracle, an independent verifier, a 28/28 result and a mutation arm were all present. The correct action was therefore to VERIFY that landing independently, not to re-implement it.
why_this_matters: A ruling authorises work; it does not assert the work is outstanding. Conversely, the existence of a deliverable does not make the deliverable correct. 'Authorised', 'carded', 'present' and 'correct' are four separate judgements and each was made separately here.

self_inflicted_criterion_errors_recorded.error: guessed the interface signature: called demand_key(request={...}) expecting a dict back
self_inflicted_criterion_errors_recorded.symptom: TypeError: demand_key() got an unexpected keyword argument 'request'
self_inflicted_criterion_errors_recorded.actual_signature: demand_key(*, source_sha256, review_policy, role_set, identity: dict) -> str; identity is built by the separate request_identity() function and the return value is a hex digest
self_inflicted_criterion_errors_recorded.fix: read the source to establish the real signature rather than bending the subject to my guess; and since a digest exposes no members, read the key's members from demand_key's source literal while also running a behavioural check
self_inflicted_criterion_errors_recorded.lesson: #23 in this project's series -- a criterion must be written to the subject's REAL shape, and the only reliable source of that shape is the subject's own source, not my impression of it

self_inflicted_criterion_errors_recorded.error: transcription passed off as verification, and then a text comparison tripped on formatting
self_inflicted_criterion_errors_recorded.symptom: (a) P-5 initially only read failed == 10 out of provenance.json; (b) after making it really run, observed_matches_recorded_red_set came out False while the red SETS were identical in case, count and order
self_inflicted_criterion_errors_recorded.root_cause: (a) re-reading a number out of a record proves the record contains that text, not that the mutation turns anything red; (b) sorted() over raw strings was tripped by one incidental omission of a parenthetical suffix
self_inflicted_criterion_errors_recorded.fix: (a) actually re-run the mutation and observe; (b) compare a normalised form and state why the normalisation is legitimate, then prove with negative controls that it still rejects a substantive difference
self_inflicted_criterion_errors_recorded.lesson: #24 in this project's series -- when a gate goes red, classify it: is the DATA wrong or the CRITERION wrong? Fix the right one and say which. Do not delete the check to get green, and do not loosen it silently.

self_inflicted_criterion_errors_recorded.details: a field named recorded_mutant_passed actually asserted that the recorded `passed` COUNT equalled 18 -- i.e. it read as the opposite of what it asserted
self_inflicted_criterion_errors_recorded.lesson: a field name is part of the criterion; a name that reverses the meaning will lead the next reader to the wrong conclusion
